title: Pitches from women that mention the educational needs of their children or a brighter future for them accelerate funding.
Direct thank you to lenders may accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Female borrowers who specify the occupation of their husband may fund faster.
Male borrowers who mention long-term goals of asset acquisition, such as land, may fund faster.
Mentioning specific family support needs, such as children's education, predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who name their specific institutional partner (e.g., BRAC, VisionFund) may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention previous loans from NWTF may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention children's educational needs or specific ages may fund faster.
Pitches from women that emphasize family composition or marital status tend to fund more slowly than those focusing on professional history.
Female borrowers who mention a supportive husband helping with repayment may fund more slowly.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayment predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Providing specific operational or inventory details predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who specify the number of years their business has been running fund faster.
Mentioning specific details about the number or ages of children predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
